property_summary: Invariant: After a successful external Put call by any EOA sending value, the caller's recorded Acc balance in the reference increases by exactly the sent value and is >= previous balance; the mutant that omits setting locked_ = true can be re-entered during the Put call (via fallback of a malicious callee) and thus cause the final recorded balance to differ (not equal to previous+value) for some inputs.

For every call to Put by any caller sending value, the caller's recorded Acc.balance increases exactly by the sent value (final balance == previous balance + msg.value); the mutant that omits setting locked_ = true allows reentrancy during Put and can make the final stored balance differ from previous+msg.value for some inputs.

For any caller and any amount sent to Put, the contract's recorded Acc[caller].balance after Put must equal the caller's previous stored balance plus msg.value; the mutant omitting locked_=true allows reentrant calls during Put and can make the final stored balance differ for some inputs (attacker and amount).

For any caller and any nonzero ether amount, a call to Put increments Acc[caller].balance by exactly msg.value (final balance == previous balance + msg.value); the mutant omitting locked_ = true permits reentrancy during Put and can cause the final stored balance to differ for some attacker and amount.

For any caller and any ether amount, after calling Put the recorded Acc[caller].balance equals the previous balance plus msg.value; the mutant that omits setting locked_ = true permits reentrancy during Put (via a malicious recipient) and can make the final stored balance differ for some inputs.

For any caller and any Ether amount and unlockTime, after calling Put(unlockTime) the contract's Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is at least the current block.timestamp (i.e., cannot be set to a past time); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it to a past timestamp, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller, after Put(...) completes the stored unlockTime for that caller is >= block.timestamp (the contract never sets unlockTime to a past timestamp); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it < block.timestamp for some fuzzed inputs and so violates this property.

For any caller and any Put(_unlockTime, value), the reference contract ensures the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is never decreased below the pre-call block.timestamp (it becomes max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime allows it to be set below block.timestamp for some fuzzed inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any inputs, calling Put(_unlockTime) on the reference contract always sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to a value that is at least the block.timestamp observed at the time of the Put call (i.e. the contract never stores an unlockTime earlier than the current timestamp); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it to an earlier timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any Put(_unlockTime) call, the contract stores Acc[caller].unlockTime >= the block.timestamp at the time of the call (it never sets unlockTime to a past timestamp); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this rule.

For any caller and any msg.value, calling Put(...) on the correct contract increases (or leaves unchanged only when msg.value == 0) the caller's stored balance by exactly msg.value (i.e., Acc[msg.sender].balance after Put == old_balance + msg.value); the mutant overwrites balance with msg.value and therefore violates this when the caller already had a non-zero prior balance and msg.value != old_balance + msg.value.
